text: {"claims":[{"id":"c1","evidence":[{"sid":"P1.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P2.S1","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P1.S0 states the 64-table join cap; P2.S1 states there is no mechanism to raise or lower the join-table limit, so run-time change is impossible."},{"id":"c3","evidence":[{"sid":"P4.S2","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P3.S1","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P4.S2 makes the sqlite3_limit call a no-op when the compile-time depth is 0; P3.S1 says a zero value means no limit is enforced."},{"id":"c4","evidence":[{"sid":"P0.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P0.S2","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P0.S3","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P0.S0 introduces per-connection sqlite3_limit; P0.S2 gives the browser/history/JavaScript example; P0.S3 says trusted internal databases can be unconstrained while untrusted ones are tightly limited."},{"id":"c6","evidence":[{"sid":"P6.S2","rel":"refutes"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P6.S2 ties the approximate 2e+13 row ceiling to a 281 TB database, not to the 17.5 TB size from P5.S2; the claim assigns that ceiling to the smaller database."},{"id":"c7","evidence":[{"sid":"P5.S2","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P5.S3","rel":"entails"}],"check":{"kind":"arith","expr":"65536 / 4096","op":"==","value":"16"},"reasoning":"P5.S2 and P5.S3 provide the page sizes and corresponding approximate maximum database sizes; the page-size ratio is 16, consistent with the claimed scaling."},{"id":"c8","evidence":[{"sid":"P7.S2","rel":"refutes"},{"sid":"P7.S3","rel":"refutes"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P7.S2 says increases are expected to be rare, and P7.S3 says lower limits are more commonly wanted, opposite to the claim that most applications need higher limits."}]}
